## Open Scholarship news at SFU

### Creative Knowledge Mobilization Workshop Series

::: {.feature image="os_newsletter-nov2026-km_workshops.jpg" alt="Creative Knowledge Mobilization Workshop Series, Workshop 2: Podcasting. November 10, 2026, 10:00 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 3:30 p.m., Unnamed PubLab (Room HC 2960), SFU Harbour Centre, 515 West Hastings St. Instructors: Dr. Hannah McGregor and Garth Mullins." link="https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/creative-knowledge-mobilization-workshop-series-podcasting-tickets-2002826996461?aff=oddtdtcreator"}


The SFU Community-Engaged Research Initiative, the SFU Knowledge Mobilization
Hub and the UBC Public Humanities Hub are hosting a series of workshops
exploring creative approaches to knowledge mobilization. Designed for
researchers, graduate students, practitioners and community partners, the
series introduces practical skills for translating research into engaging,
accessible and impactful public-facing formats. On November 10, the theme is
podcasting!

::: {.event date="2026-11-10" time="10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m." place="SFU Harbour Centre, Unnamed PubLab (Room HC 2960)"}
#### Podcasting as Movement Journalism

Activist, author and podcaster Garth Mullins will discuss his work on the
podcast *Crackdown* and introduce the idea of “movement journalism.”
:::

::: {.event date="2026-11-10" time="1:00 to 3:30 p.m." place="SFU Harbour Centre, Unnamed PubLab (Room HC 2960)"}
#### How to Create a Research Podcast

Dr. Hannah McGregor will lead a practical, hands-on session exploring how to
develop a podcast grounded in research and community engagement.
:::

We absolutely LOVE to see these initiatives integrating the open movement at
SFU and strongly encourage you to sign up! Plus, lunch will be provided!

[Register here](https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/creative-knowledge-mobilization-workshop-series-podcasting-tickets-2002826996461?aff=oddtdtcreator){.button}
:::

### Celebrating Open Education at SFU

::: {.feature image="sfu_oe-cop.jpg" alt="SFU Open Education Community of Practice" link="https://events.sfu.ca/event/50485-sfu-open-education-community-celebration"}

Open educational resources (OER) and practices (OEP) make learning more
affordable, accessible and open for SFU students. On **November 10, from
12:30 to 2:00 p.m.**, join us for a celebration recognizing SFU instructors
and practitioners who are using, developing and supporting OER and OEP for
teaching and learning!

Whether you’re already using OER in your teaching, supporting open education
in your work, or curious about getting started, you’re warmly invited to
celebrate SFU’s growing open education community.

The event is hosted by the Open Education Community of Practice and
[Open Scholarship Framework](https://www.sfu.ca/research/research-impact/performance-excellence/open-science.html)
teams here at SFU. Coffee and light refreshments will be provided.

[Learn more and register](https://events.sfu.ca/event/50485-sfu-open-education-community-celebration){.button}

Interested in staying involved with the Open Education Community of Practice?
[Join our Canvas space](https://canvas.sfu.ca/enroll/3H3PHW)!
:::

::: highlight
### Open Scholarship Champions: new round open!

We’re still accepting applications for the
[Center for Open Science’s self-paced courses](https://centerforopenscience.catalog.instructure.com/)!
If you want to become an Open Scholarship Champion, we will offer you a full
scholarship to complete one or more of these training courses and get a
certificate.

Grantees have until **May 1, 2027** to complete their training and until
**August 1, 2027** to complete a project of their choice.

If you’re unable or prefer not to take a COS course, you can still
participate! Simply complete another open scholarship training and provide
proof of completion. All participants, whichever training they choose, have
the same August 1, 2027 deadline for their projects.

[Apply for a COS seat](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/0yKcdeN6wZ){.button} [Register as a Champion](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/bSfwvHRVaR){.button .secondary}

*This opportunity is recognized on the Co-Curricular Record (CCR), an
official university document that tracks your co-curricular involvement at
SFU. [Learn more about the Co-Curricular Record](http://www.sfu.ca/students/get-involved/recognition/co-curricular-record).*
:::

### New open killer whale sound catalogue

From [SFU News](https://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2026/09/new-sound-catalogue-reveals-who-s-who-in-the-world-of-killer-wha.html):

> “A new open-access catalogue of whale calls will help researchers and orca
> enthusiasts identify distinct killer whale populations, clans and family
> groups by their vocalizations alone. Developed at Simon Fraser University,
> the Orca Call Catalogue serves as a field guide to killer whale calls,
> pulling decades of recordings into a searchable online library for the
> first time, says John Ford, scientist emeritus at Fisheries and Oceans
> Canada.”

This project shows how engaged our community is in open scholarship
practices! Shout out to the [Research Computing Group](https://www.rcg.sfu.ca/)
for providing the infrastructure needed for this project.

If you have a project that you’d like to make open,
[reach out to us](mailto:open_scholarship@sfu.ca) and we’ll help you figure
out a plan to make it happen!

#### Drop by to chat about open scholarship

We have open office hours online every Monday (11 a.m. to 1 p.m.) and
Wednesday (1 to 3 p.m.). Book a 30-minute chat if you have questions about
open scholarship practices. We can connect you with the right support
service at SFU or brainstorm solutions together.
